tour.name: Mont-Saint-Michel Private Day Trip from Paris: The Abbey, the Bay & a Normandy Village
tour.subtitle: A long private day to one of the wonders of the Western world with your own driver and a licensed guide: the Benedictine abbey on its rock, the medieval village, the bay and its tides, lunch with Normandy specialities and a stop in a half-timbered village on the way.

tour.overview:
Mont-Saint-Michel rises from a vast bay on the border of Normandy and Brittany, a granite island crowned by an abbey whose spire reaches 170 metres above the sands. Monks settled here in the 8th century, after the archangel Michael was said to have appeared to the bishop of Avranches, and for a thousand years pilgrims crossed the bay on foot at low tide to reach it. The tides here are among the highest in Europe, with up to 14 metres between low and high water. Mont-Saint-Michel and its bay have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1979.

This private day takes you there from Paris in a comfortable car, so you can rest on the way. Your licensed guide shows you the abbey, the village and the ramparts, and explains how the bay has been restored to make the Mont an island again. On the way back you stop at a cider farm and in one of the prettiest villages of Normandy.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 14 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Paris
• Type: private tour with car and driver; licensed guide at Mont-Saint-Michel
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; the abbey is reached by about 350 steps

WHAT YOU SEE
• The bay and the view of the Mont from the new bridge.
• The Grande Rue and the medieval village.
• The abbey church, the cloister and the refectory of the Marvel.
• The ramparts.
• A cider farm in the Pays d'Auge.
• Honfleur or Beuvron-en-Auge.

WHY THIS WORKS
We leave Paris early to reach the Mont before the midday crowds and adjust the day to the tide tables, so you see the bay at its most spectacular.

WHO IT SUITS
Anyone who wants to see Mont-Saint-Michel without spending the night, families and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
If you have two days, we strongly recommend a night at the Mont or in Normandy, combined with the D-Day beaches.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive is about 4 hours each way. Cars must park on the mainland; a free shuttle bus or a 40-minute walk across the bridge takes you to the island. Never walk on the sands without a certified guide: the tides and quicksand are dangerous.

days.name: Drive to Normandy, Mont-Saint-Michel abbey and village, the bay, a cider farm and a Normandy village
days.description:
What to expect: the abbey on its rock in the sea and the Normandy countryside, with a private car, a licensed guide, lunch and a cider tasting.

Your driver collects you at your hotel at 6:30 for the drive west through the plains and hedgerows of Normandy, about four hours with a coffee break. You arrive at about 10:45 and see the Mont rising from the bay, then take the shuttle bus or walk across the footbridge opened in 2014, part of a project that removed the old causeway so the tides could flow freely around the island again.

Your guide meets you at the gate. You climb the Grande Rue, the single street of the medieval village, lined with timber houses and once full of inns for pilgrims, and continue up the long stairways to the abbey. The abbey church stands on the very top of the rock, with a Romanesque nave and a Gothic choir rebuilt in the 15th century. On the north side, the three-storey Gothic building called La Merveille, the Marvel, was built in the 13th century in only 25 years: you walk through the cloister, suspended between sea and sky, the refectory filled with light, the Knights' Hall and the crypts, and see the great wheel once turned by prisoners to hoist supplies when the abbey served as a prison after the Revolution.

For lunch you try the Mont's famous puffed omelette, first served by Mère Poulard in the 1880s, or salt-meadow lamb, raised on the grass of the bay. You walk part of the ramparts with views over the sands, where at low tide the sea retreats as far as 15 kilometres and returns, as Victor Hugo wrote, at the speed of a galloping horse. In the afternoon you drive back east, stopping at a cider farm in the Pays d'Auge for a tasting of cider, pommeau and Calvados, and in Beuvron-en-Auge, one of the most beautiful villages in France, or the old harbour of Honfleur, depending on the time. You arrive back at your hotel in Paris at about 20:30.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
06:30 – Pick-up at your hotel in Paris.
10:45 – Arrival at Mont-Saint-Michel, shuttle to the island.
11:00 – Village and abbey with your guide (about 2 hours).
13:15 – Lunch.
14:30 – Ramparts and free time.
15:30 – Drive towards the Pays d'Auge.
17:15 – Cider farm tasting.
18:00 – Beuvron-en-Auge or Honfleur.
20:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• We check the tide tables when planning; on days of very high tides the Mont becomes an island for a short time, a spectacular sight.
• A guided crossing of the bay on foot at low tide can be arranged on a separate day.
• The abbey has many stairs and is not suitable for wheelchairs.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide at the Mont, abbey ticket, lunch, cider tasting, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks with lunch, dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is it too long for a day trip?
faq.answer: It is a long day of about 14 hours, with roughly 8 hours in the car. The car is comfortable and you can sleep on the way. If you can, we recommend spending a night in Normandy instead.

faq.question: Can we combine Mont-Saint-Michel with the D-Day beaches?
faq.answer: Not comfortably in one day from Paris. We offer a two-day version with a night in Bayeux or at the Mont.

faq.question: Is the guide with us all day?
faq.answer: Your driver accompanies you all day. A licensed guide joins you at Mont-Saint-Michel for the abbey and village, where guiding is required to be licensed.

faq.question: Are the entrance tickets included?
faq.answer: Yes, the abbey ticket. The shuttle from the car park to the island is free.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, lunch on the Mont with a Normandy speciality. Vegetarian and other diets can be arranged.

faq.question: How many stairs are there?
faq.answer: About 350 steps from the village to the abbey, plus stairs inside. Take your time; there are places to rest along the way.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the castle-like abbey, the ramparts and the tides. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: The village and abbey are steep with many steps and are not accessible to wheelchairs. The view of the Mont from the bridge and the Normandy villages are easy.

faq.question: Can we walk on the sands?
faq.answer: Only with a certified bay guide, because of fast tides and quicksand. A guided crossing can be arranged as a separate experience.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes for steps and cobbles, and a windproof jacket: it is often windy on the Mont, even in summer.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Spring and autumn have the most dramatic tides and fewer crowds; summer is busy but has long evenings.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 72 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
